task: Review CPU/shared-Float32 six fixture generation and harness exact masks/channel metrics; preserve deliberately unsupported near-field behavior.

revision.head: 9257b6dc8b0b7bb5fe0a1b3fd076d6d2cde69419
revision.justification: HEAD advances documentation/state only. git diff --exit-code against source candidate returned 0 for all reviewed source/harness/workflow files. Existing unrelated working-tree changes were not modified.

tests.check: Read-only fixture generation and consumer inspection
tests.result: All six named scenes are generated at 96x64 using shared StudyComputeInput and CPU ReferenceStudyRenderer. Header writes little-endian width/height/row counts/unsupported count; Float32 bit patterns precede the exact reference RGBA. Explicit binary validity mask is encoded into fixture alpha, leaving the original opaque StudyImage untouched.

Header and row counts, finite inputs, exact reference byte length, alpha values, magenta unsupported sentinels and reference count consistency are checked. Every invalid-mask position must match. RGB metrics cover exactly width*height*3 channels with mean <= 1 and fraction(error > 4) <= 0.005; optional maximum channel error is independent. CI uses pipefail.

tests.check: Read existing fresh study-kernel.log and core-environment.log
tests.result: Six PASS lines: dark/hard/warm-rotated mean 0 max 0; soft/translated mean 5.42535e-05 max 1; near-field mean 0 max 0 and invalid 84/84. All six have fraction >4 = 0 and invalid-mask-mismatches = 0. Other five invalid counts are 0/0. Environment records Ubuntu 24.04.5 x86_64 Linux, Swift 6.4.2, source revision 4d0c67d258be802f048e74616cabcdf903e2b59d.

tests.check: Near-field semantics and backend boundary source inspection
tests.result: Near-field remains among all six and exercises unsupported pixels; the twelve image-fixture zero-unsupported requirement does not apply to this deliberate parity case. Production Metal eligibility routes this scene to CPU. The parity-only renderValidationFixture entry point retains this scene and is used by native validation.

No test, compiler, generator, renderer, harness, or native suite rerun. Existing Linux C++ shared-Float32 log is host evidence, not actual Metal execution, iPhone performance, or physical calibration. No new native or image-review claim.

outcome: No material defect found. Generator/consumer framing, six-fixture membership, exact invalid masks, channel metrics and fresh host evidence are consistent with the m02-m03-code-v2 parity contract. Native Metal evidence remains separate.
